channel.title: Ghosxt Blog: Managed IT & Cybersecurity for the Central Coast
channel.description: Practical IT, cybersecurity, and compliance guidance for small businesses on California's Central Coast, from an engineer with DoD infrastructure experience.

item.title: Password Spray Attacks: How One Slow-Motion Guess Slips Past Lockout Policies (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Password spraying tries one common password against hundreds of accounts instead of hammering one account with thousands of guesses, so it never trips a lockout policy. How the attack works and what actually stops it.

item.title: Insider Threats: The Cybersecurity Risk Already Inside Your Business (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Most small business security spending targets outside attackers, but a careless click, a disgruntled ex-employee, or a departing hire's laptop can do just as much damage. How insider threats actually happen and what stops them.

item.title: Ransomware Negotiation: Should Your Small Business Ever Pay? (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: What actually happens during a ransomware negotiation, why paying doesn't guarantee your data back, and the questions a small business should answer before wiring a cent.

item.title: Social Media Account Takeover: How Hackers Hijack Your Business Facebook or Instagram Page (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A hacked Facebook or Instagram business page gets used to scam your customers, drain your ad budget, or held for ransom. How the takeover happens and how small businesses get pages back and lock them down.

item.title: IoT Device Security for Small Business: The Hidden Attack Surface (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Smart cameras, thermostats, and printers on your business network often run default passwords and years-old firmware. How IoT devices become an entry point and how to lock them down.

item.title: Fileless Malware: The Attack That Leaves Nothing for Antivirus to Find (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Fileless malware and living-off-the-land attacks run entirely in memory using tools already on your PC, so antivirus never sees a file to scan.

item.title: VoIP Toll Fraud: How a Hacked Phone System Runs Up a Five-Figure Bill Overnight (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A hacked business phone system can rack up thousands in international calls in a single weekend. How VoIP toll fraud works and how to stop it.

item.title: USB Drop Attacks: How a "Lost" Flash Drive Becomes a Ransomware Foothold (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A USB drive left in a parking lot can hand an attacker a foothold before anyone clicks a link. How USB drop attacks work and how to stop them.

item.title: Malvertising: How Fake Software Ads Are Infecting Small Businesses (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Malicious search ads impersonate PuTTY, Zoom, and other downloads, infecting employees before the real site loads. How malvertising works.

item.title: ClickFix: The Fake CAPTCHA Attack Tricking Employees Into Infecting Their Own PC (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: ClickFix pages pose as a CAPTCHA or Zoom error, tricking employees into pasting a command into Windows Run. How it bypasses antivirus.

item.title: Evil Twin Wi-Fi: How Fake Hotspots Steal Data From Remote Workers (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Evil twin Wi-Fi hotspots copy a real network's name to intercept logins and files from remote and traveling employees. How the attack works and how to stop it.

item.title: Session Hijacking: How Stolen Cookies Let Attackers Skip Past MFA (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Session hijacking steals the cookie that proves you're logged in, letting attackers skip MFA without a password. How it works and how to stop it.

item.title: Typosquatting: How Lookalike Domains Impersonate Your Business (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Typosquatting uses lookalike domains to impersonate your business or your vendors for phishing and invoice fraud. How it works and how to stop it in 2026.

item.title: SIM Swapping: How Attackers Hijack Your Phone Number to Get Into Business Accounts (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: SIM swapping hijacks your phone number to intercept SMS codes and reset passwords. How it works, the warning signs, and the fixes that stop it in 2026.

item.title: Credential Stuffing: How Reused Passwords Let Attackers Into Your Business Accounts (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Credential stuffing doesn't hack your business. It logs in with a password your employee reused elsewhere. How the attack works, and how to stop it.

item.title: Mobile Device Management (MDM) for Small Business: When You Actually Need It (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: BYOD policies cover personal phones, but company-owned devices and field teams often outgrow that. What MDM does, and how to roll it out.

item.title: Passkeys for Small Business: Should You Ditch Passwords in 2026?
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Passkeys now work across Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and banking apps, and can't be phished. What they are and a realistic rollout plan.

item.title: LegacyHive: Nightmare-Eclipse's New Windows Zero-Day, Explained
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: LegacyHive: Nightmare-Eclipse's new Windows privilege-escalation zero-day, unpatched with no CVE yet. What it does and what to do this week.

item.title: Vishing: How Voice Phishing Calls Are Scamming Small Businesses in 2026
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A phone call claiming to be your bank, the IRS, or your IT department is one of the oldest scams, and it still works. Why caller ID can't be trusted.

item.title: July 2026 Patch Tuesday: A Record 570 Fixes, 3 Zero-Days, and What an SMB Should Patch First
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: July 2026 Patch Tuesday: a record 570 fixes and 3 zero-days, including AD FS and SharePoint flaws. What a small business should patch first.

item.title: AI Agents at Work: The Non-Human Identity Risk Small Businesses Aren't Managing
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: AI agents can send email, book meetings, and update your CRM using real credentials. Why non-human identities are a growing small-business risk.

item.title: Zero Trust Security for Small Business: What It Actually Means in 2026
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Zero Trust gets called a buzzword, but the model is simple: never trust, always verify. What it means for a 10-person business, and where to start.

item.title: ADA Website Accessibility for Small Business: What California Law Requires (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Accessibility demand letters are hitting California businesses, and the Unruh Act raises the stakes. What ADA and WCAG 2.1 AA require.

item.title: Smishing: How Text Message Phishing Is Hitting Small Businesses in 2026
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Fake delivery texts, toll bills, and payroll alerts: smishing skips your spam filter and lands on employee phones. How it works and how to stop it.

item.title: How Much Does a Small Business Website Cost in 2026? Real Numbers
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Real 2026 website pricing for small businesses: what a 5-page site, a full site, and e-commerce cost, and why $500 or $15,000 sites are usually wrong.

item.title: 9 Signs Your Small Business Website Is Costing You Customers (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A slow, broken, or outdated website sends customers to competitors. The 9 warning signs it's time to fix or rebuild, and which are security risks.

item.title: OAuth App Phishing: How Attackers Get Into Microsoft 365 Without Stealing a Password (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Attackers don't need your password or MFA code, just a click on 'Accept' for a fake app. How OAuth consent phishing bypasses MFA, and how to stop it.

item.title: California Data Breach Notification Law: What Small Businesses Must Do After a Breach (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: California's breach notification law applies no matter how small your business is. What counts as a reportable breach, and the real CPRA lawsuit risk.

item.title: BYOD for Small Business: Securing Personal Phones and Laptops Without Locking Down Everyone's Devices (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Your team is already checking company email on personal phones, policy or not. What a BYOD policy needs to cover, and how to secure devices.

item.title: The Seasonal Worker IT Checklist: Onboarding and Offboarding Summer Staff Without Leaving Accounts Open
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Harvest crews and summer hires need system access, and few businesses ever turn it back off. Onboarding and offboarding checklist for seasonal staff.
